title: What a wrapped app cannot do, and finding that out before the store does

videos.script:
This lesson is the one that saves you from an expensive mistake. {{mistake}} A wrapped app can be refused by a store, or kept by nobody, and both are usually found out late.

Two people judge the wrapper. {{judges}} The reviewer, who asks whether it is more than a website in a frame. And the person who installs it, who notices every place it does not behave like an app.

Some limits are polish, and you can fix them with web work. Others are out of the WebView's reach. {{reach}} A widget. A watch. Work while the app is closed.

Then you measure. {{measure}} The planner with five thousand sessions, on a processor slowed down like a cheap phone. A tap takes about a second. And the measurement says something you might not expect: the slowness is the planner's design, not the WebView's.

Last, a checklist, and three questions to decide with. {{decide}} For most apps, the answer is to wrap. The lesson is how to know when it is not.
